cohort_total_n_excerpt: 4208 older men aged 70-88 years in Perth, Western Australia.
reason: The study prospectively evaluates new prostate cancer diagnoses overall. The abstract does not report an aggressive prostate cancer endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In multivariate competing risks proportional hazards models, every 10 nmol/l decrease in 25(OH)D concentration was associated with a 4% reduction in prostate cancer incidence (sub-hazard ratio [SHR] 0.96, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.92-1.00).
estimate_classifications.reason: The underlying published estimate concerns overall incident prostate cancer. The supplied row is the reciprocal orientation of the abstract's SHR for each 10 nmol/l decrease.
